greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. We gather in this quiet space to place our hearts before the Lord, who knows us better than we know ourselves.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you call us to sit at your feet and listen: Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you reveal the Father’s grace to the humble: Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you guide us along your everlasting way: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Guide me, Lord, along the everlasting way.
homily:
We often imagine that our lives are defined by the sheer volume of our activity. We measure our worth by the weight of our tasks, the length of our to-do lists, and the frantic pace at which we move from one responsibility to the next. We are, by nature, a people of the 'serving.' We want to provide, we want to fix, we want to build, and we want to ensure that those we love are cared for. We pride ourselves on our industry. We believe that if we are busy enough, if we are vigilant enough, we can keep the world spinning on its axis and keep the people we love safe within the walls we have built.

Then, we encounter a scene like the one in today’s Gospel. Jesus enters a village. He is welcomed into a home—a home that sounds very much like any of ours. There is Martha, who is 'burdened with much serving.' And there is Mary, who is simply sitting at the feet of the Lord. It is a scene that has been debated for centuries, often framed as a competition between the active life and the contemplative life. But look closer. Look at the ache in Martha’s voice. She says, 'Lord, do you not care?'

That is the question that haunts the human heart in the wake of great loss. 'Lord, do you not care?' It is the question that rises up when the rhythm of a home is shattered. It is the question that sits in the silence of an empty chair, or in the stillness of a room where a boy’s laughter used to echo. Martha is not just complaining about chores; she is expressing the fundamental human fear that we are alone in our burden, that our effort is unseen, and that the things we value most are slipping through our fingers despite our best attempts to hold them tight.

Think of Benjamin Vo. Think of the way he moved through his short, beautiful life with such a brilliant, focused intensity. He was a boy who loved the mechanics of the world—the way code could build a digital kingdom, the way a Boeing 737 could master the sky, the way a logic puzzle could be solved. He was a builder. He was a student of how things work. He was a boy who looked at the horizon and saw not just distance, but destination. He was a boy who loved his father’s stories, who shared in the joy of a kitchen filled with the bustle of baking, and who carried a quiet, fierce loyalty to his brother, Ryan. Ben lived with an energy that was always reaching, always learning, always trying to understand the world so that he could participate in it more fully.

But the Gospel today reminds us that there is something deeper than the work of our hands. Jesus does not rebuke Martha for her love; He rebukes her for her anxiety. He says, 'Martha, Martha, you are anxious and worried about many things. There is need of only one thing.' What is that one thing? It is not a task. It is not a project. It is not a result. The 'one thing' is the presence of the Lord Himself. It is the willingness to stop, to sit, and to be held in the gaze of the One who made us.

Alan and Thao, I know the weight of these months. I know the feeling of wanting to do something, anything, to restore the order of your world. You remember the way Ben would look at you with that bright, silly grin, especially when he was caught in a moment of pure, unadulterated joy—like when he tried that spicy Pad Thai in Bangkok and just giggled at the absurdity of it. You remember the way he would offer his own resources, like that time he wanted to give his entire piggy bank to help his Uncle William. That wasn't a transaction. It was a reflection of a heart that understood that we are here to give, not to hoard. That is the boy you raised. That is the legacy of love he left behind. And that legacy is not a burden you have to manage; it is a grace you have been given.

There is a profound truth in our first reading today from Saint Paul. He talks about how God had set him apart 'from my mother’s womb.' Paul was a man who had been a zealot, a man who had been obsessed with his own 'serving,' his own righteousness, his own way of doing things. He had to be brought to his knees before he could see that the only thing that mattered was the grace of Christ. He had to stop fighting, stop building, and start receiving. Paul’s life was completely transformed when he realized that he was not the author of his own mission. God was. And God is the author of Benjamin’s life as well.

When you feel that sudden, sharp ache of his absence, do not be afraid. That ache is simply your love looking for a place to land. Let it land on the promise of the Resurrection. Let it land on the certainty that Benjamin is not in the past; he is in the future. He is at the destination, waiting for you to complete the journey. He is not a project that was cut short; he is a life that has been gathered into the harvest of God’s own love. You are not being asked to understand the mysteries of the universe. You are being asked to trust the One who holds the stars in place and who holds Benjamin in the palm of His hand.

Ryan, you are the one who carries that peace now. You are the brother who knows the rhythm of Ben’s heart. You know the secrets of the games he coded, the joy he found in the simple things, the way he looked at the world with wonder. When you walk into a room, you are carrying that legacy. You are carrying the curiosity, the kindness, and the love that you and Ben shared. You are not a brother who is walking alone. You are a brother who is walking with the strength of a love that has already arrived at the destination. Keep being the boy who is curious. Keep being the brother who knows that love is the only thing that actually lasts. You are a family of four, and that will never change. You are just living in two different rooms of the same house, and the door between them is held open by the grace of Christ.

I want to speak very gently to the ache that sometimes visits you in the quiet of the night. There is a weight that parents often carry, a stone of wondering if they missed something or could have done more. I want to lift that stone from you today. You were the parents Benjamin needed. You were his sanctuary. You were the ones who nurtured that brilliant, curious, gentle spirit. You did not miss anything. God does not look at your son’s life and find it lacking, and He does not look at your care for him and find it wanting. You are not being accused. You are being held. Let that stone fall. You are free to grieve, you are free to miss him, but you are not required to carry the burden of self-reproach. That is a weight that has no place in the kingdom of God. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him.

Think of the 'Well of Love' in Vietnam. That well is a perfect image of what you are doing. You are taking the love that was poured into Ben, and you are letting it flow into the lives of others. You are ensuring that his life is not a closed chapter, but a living, breathing, life-sustaining force. Every time you are kind, every time you choose to forgive, every time you choose to hope in the face of despair, you are allowing his legacy to refresh the world. You are turning the soil of the earth so that the Kingdom can grow. You are the ones who are keeping his light burning in a world that so often forgets to look up.

We are on this earth, as the Psalm says, to see the bounty of the Lord in the land of the living. Sometimes that land feels like a desert. Sometimes it feels like we are waiting for a harvest that will never come. But the Gospel tells us that we are watched over. We are guarded. We are guided. We are never out of the sight of the Father. When the days feel long and the silence feels heavy, remember that you are not being asked to understand the mysteries of the universe. You are being asked to trust the One who holds the stars in place and who holds Benjamin in the palm of His hand. You are being asked to live in such a way that his memory continues to be a blessing to everyone you meet.

So today, carry this away with you: you are never alone. You are a family that is being held by the same hands that hold the universe. When you see a bird in flight, or a plane climbing into the clouds, don't just see a machine or a creature; see a sign of the freedom that Benjamin now knows. See a sign of the promise that you are walking toward. Keep your eyes on the horizon. The journey is not over; it is simply continuing in a new, more glorious way. And one day, when the long road reaches the end, you will look up and see him waiting for you, and the joy will be beyond all reckoning.

Take this with you: you are a family of four, and that will never change. The geography of your life has shifted, but the bond of your love is eternal. Keep the 'Well of Love' flowing in his name. Keep the kindness moving. Keep the dream alive. And when you walk out those doors, look up at the sky. Remember that he is not in the dust. He is in the light. He is waiting for you, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile that you remember so vividly. That smile is a sign. It is a sign that the harvest is coming, and that the One who started this good work in you will surely bring it to completion. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that you are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love you above all things, and I desire to receive you into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive you sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace you as if you were already there and unite myself wholly to you. Never permit me to be separated from you. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may His face shine upon you and give you peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Benjamin, and for all who have gone before us marked with the sign of faith, that they may rest forever in the light and peace of Christ, we pray to the Lord.
For all who are grieving and carrying the heavy cross of loss, that God may console them, strengthen their hearts, and give them the hope of the Resurrection, we pray to the Lord.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Brothers and sisters:
You heard of my former way of life in Judaism,
how I persecuted the Church of God beyond measure
and tried to destroy it, 
and progressed in Judaism
beyond many of my contemporaries among my race,
since I was even more a zealot for my ancestral traditions.
But when he, who from my mother’s womb had set me apart
and called me through his grace,
was pleased to reveal his Son to me,
so that I might proclaim him to the Gentiles,
I did not immediately consult flesh and blood,
nor did I go up to Jerusalem
to those who were Apostles before me;
rather, I went into Arabia and then returned to Damascus.Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to confer with Cephas
and remained with him for fifteen days.
But I did not see any other of the Apostles,
only James the brother of the Lord.
(As to what I am writing to you, behold,
before God, I am not lying.)
Then I went into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
And I was unknown personally to the churches of Judea
that are in Christ;
they only kept hearing that “the one who once was persecuting us
is now preaching the faith he once tried to destroy.”
So they glorified God because of me.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (24b) Guide me, Lord, along the everlasting way.
O LORD, you have probed me and you know me;
you know when I sit and when I stand;
you understand my thoughts from afar.
My journeys and my rest you scrutinize,
with all my ways you are familiar.
R. Guide me, Lord, along the everlasting way.
Truly you have formed my inmost being;
you knit me in my mother’s womb.
I give you thanks that I am fearfully, wonderfully made;
wonderful are your works.
R. Guide me, Lord, along the everlasting way.
My soul also you knew full well;
nor was my frame unknown to you
When I was made in secret,
when I was fashioned in the depths of the earth.
R. Guide me, Lord, along the everlasting way.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
Jesus entered a village 
where a woman whose name was Martha welcomed him.
She had a sister named Mary
who sat beside the Lord at his feet listening to him speak. 
Martha, burdened with much serving, came to him and said,
“Lord, do you not care
that my sister has left me by myself to do the serving? 
Tell her to help me.” 
The Lord said to her in reply,
“Martha, Martha, you are anxious and worried about many things. 
There is need of only one thing. 
Mary has chosen the better part
and it will not be taken from her.”

day: Tuesday of the Twenty-seventh Week in Ordinary Time

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben, Trustin visited you today and left you a few airplane cards—we're putting them in your room for you. Please pray for Trustin and his family to stay healthy and strong. Be a guardian angel to Trustin and Ryan as they go through school, and help guide their steps through every year to come.
